newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee stays mixed by close, Jan shines.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee stays mixed by close, Jan shines.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures stayed mixed up to the close as Asian origin and speculative selling countered roaster buying at the lows.
Traders said benchmark January was the only gainer on the nearbys, helped by industry buying and prompted by further New York strength on a further draw in exchange-certified stocks.
By the close, the second-month January contract was $9 up at $1,400 a tonne after ranging between $1,392 and $1,405.
The closely-watch Nov/Jan spread, a barometer of nearby supply availability, narrowed slightly to end at $122 from Monday's $130 finish.
Traders said the spot position was pressured by fresh origin selling from the Far East especially Vietnam.
"There's fresh coffee coming in that people reckon will be in time to grade and put against November," said one. "With the high premium it's really worth it."
November finished down $2 at $1,522. Turnover on the exchange reached 4,157 lots.

As expected, New York arabica coffee futures jumped in early business on news of the stock drawdown which came after the market closed on Monday. But it pared gains towards the midday close on heavy profit-taking.
The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange reported a 4,036 60-kg bag fall in certified stocks to 1,547 bags in the week ended last Friday, the lowest since the CSCE began tracking inventories in 1980.
But traders said more bullish news is that there is no coffee pending grading or recertification.
"The news might have an effect of bringing in more panic into New York," another trader said.
